raw_response:
I have farmed here a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked for me last year and what I saw in nearby fields in Quzhou. My land is 10.1 mu, not small enough to ignore yield and not big enough to waste money, so I will split it in a steady way: most land in wheat-maize, and a smaller piece in chili for cash. I have well water, so I will not be too stingy on irrigation, because if the crop dries at the wrong time, the loss is bigger than the water and electricity cost. On fertilizer, I will put enough base fertilizer first, then add more nitrogen at the key growth stage. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the crop turn pale and lose yield. For wheat, I will keep a fairly solid rate because wheat here needs a good stand before winter and then one more push at jointing. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and feed it a little heavier on nitrogen, because if maize lacks fertilizer in summer the ears stay small. Chili brings in cash, so I will manage it more carefully, with more potassium and more pesticide sprays than grain crops. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen it perform well on neighbors’ land, but I will not chase fancy things that cost too much. Labor in my house is tight because some people work off-farm, so I will choose rotary tillage where it saves time and keep the plan practical.
